answer: To curb a gale of Sybil attacks, an agent economy replaces static allowlists, an outdated relic, with continuous Verifiable Delay Function challenges. Each epoch, an agent computes a non-parallelizable sequential proof from a fresh beacon before a deadline, incurring a verifiable cost in single-thread CPU time and electricity per identity across its operational voyage. However, adversaries using faster ASICs or multi-core fleets can still scale identities with hardware spending.
